memory_update.text: Add AMZN, WMT, CART, CRTO, and RAMP to the ecommerce_retail_media_data watchlist as direct or second-order exposure to retail-media data and attribution chokepoints.

The key bottleneck is not ecommerce traffic alone; it is the combination of first-party transaction data, ad inventory, search/ranking control, checkout/fulfillment linkage, and closed-loop attribution.

Marketplace owners AMZN, WMT, and CART have stronger direct chokepoint control than ad-tech suppliers because they control purchase intent and transaction data; CRTO and RAMP are infrastructure/enabler candidates and require more evidence on revenue durability and customer concentration.

Potential additional candidates for later passes include TTD for retail-data programmatic activation, ROKU for CTV commerce-media inventory and Walmart/Instacart/Kroger partnerships, DV for ad verification, and consumer brands with heavy marketplace advertising exposure.

node: Ecommerce marketplaces, retail media networks, first-party shopper data, and search/ranking algorithms
summary: Expanded universe focuses on the scarce infrastructure around consumer ecommerce monetization: marketplaces with closed-loop shopper data, retail media networks, grocery/omnichannel commerce data, commerce-media ad-tech, and privacy-safe identity/data collaboration. The strongest direct chokepoint exposure appears in companies that own both purchase intent and ad surfaces, while second-order exposure appears in vendors that help retailers and brands activate, measure, and reconcile first-party commerce data across CTV, programmatic, and clean-room environments.
